column3: r1 was mislabeled det (sense 36558) for "so much"; that's an adverbial intensifier, re-pointed to adv sense 36564
r3 re-pointed from archaic-tagged sense 36574 to untagged synonym 36575; r5 dropped a fabricated obsolete/slang verb (mummed="to silence") and became a noun row using the chrysanthemum sense
verb POS (museuming/museumed) is a fabricated noun-to-verb backformation like "coffeeing"/"dinnering"; dropped it and gave r4/r5 real noun sentences
verb POS (musicking, "to seduce with music") is the same fabricated-backformation pattern; dropped it, r5 rewritten as a noun sentence
all 5 rows use real, correctly-sensed usages (obligation, certainty, noun "a must"); the flagged 1-form finding is a false positive since modal "must" has no inflected forms
r5 had target 'my' occurring twice in the sentence (ambiguous cloze); rewritten to a single occurrence
r2 sense corrected from "to give a name to" (36616) to "to mention, specify" (36617) to match "name your favorite animal"

r2/r3/r5 re-pointed to the specific sense each sentence actually uses instead of the generic sense; r4 switched to the noun "a natural" (innate talent) sense for POS coverage; simplified B2 vocabulary in r2
block was 5x the same adj sense; added prep, verb and adv rows since near is used at least as often as those POS in ordinary English
verb POS (the core "I need X" usage) was missing entirely; added it, replacing weaker duplicate noun rows
r2/r3 re-pointed to specific senses (test result, number); added a noun POS row ("negatives" as drawbacks); simplified B2 vocabulary in r2/r5
added a verb row ("neighbours" = is adjacent to) for POS coverage
r2 was a definitional "Never means..." sentence with B2 vocabulary; rewritten as an everyday sentence
added a noun row ("in with the new") for POS coverage
r2 was a definitional "News gives..." sentence; rewritten, and r2/r3 re-pointed to the media-usage sense
all 5 rows are genuine noun usages; verb POS (to newspaper = cover with newspaper) is real but too obscure for a learner, correctly absent
several rows mismatched adjacent-in-space vs. next-in-order senses; r4/r5 re-typed as noun and det to match their real grammar ("who is next", "next week")
r2 was a definitional "Nice means..." sentence; rewritten; added adv ("play nice") and intj ("Nice!") rows for POS coverage
all 5 rows are natural noun usages; verb POS ("to night" = to overnight) is archaic-sounding even though untagged, correctly skipped
most rows used the noun "digit/figure" sense for what are actually cardinal-quantity usages ("nine candles", "nine players"); re-pointed to num sense, kept noun only for the "page nine" label usage
r4 used the B2 word "found"; rewritten with simpler vocabulary
all 5 rows are natural, correctly-sensed num usages
r2 was a definitional "No means..." sentence; diversified across det/noun/prep/adv senses instead of 4x the same det sense
r2 was a definitional "Nobody means..." sentence; rewritten; added a noun row ("a nobody") for POS coverage
r1/r4 mislabeled directional adverb usage ("drove north") as the noun sense; r2 had target 'north' occurring twice (ambiguous cloze), rewritten; added an adj row ("the north wall") for POS coverage
